Subject: Post-call: Model fit & next steps — benchmark links

Hi Ava / John —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery: 

- Goal: Improve assistive search and generation in the product with a model that balances throughput (TPS), latency, and factuality for customer-facing responses.
- Key constraints: 2k token context support, p95 latency target < 350ms for hosted API, tighter for Dedicated.
- Primary success metric: reduction in hallucination rate on your user prompt set and sustained p95 latency within SLA at peak TPS.

Recommendations from the call:
- Pilot models: redwood-grand-7b (lower cost, good for higher TPS) and redwood-llama-13b-qa (stronger factuality on retrieval-augmented prompts).
- We ran quick internal evals against a representative prompt set and are sharing Redwood-verified performance profiles and the benchmark report attached.

Attachments/links: redwood_benchmarks_202602.pdf (high-level TPS & latency percentiles), prompt_set_v1.csv (sample prompts we discussed). Also linking the public benchmark page: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/rdw-2026-0456

Proposed next steps:
1) You share a small sample dataset (100-200 prompts + expected outputs) so we can run a focused regression-quality eval.
2) We provision a short trial (hosted credits + telemetry) and run a 48-72h throughput/latency test at your expected TPS.
3) Schedule a 45-min deep-dive demo (I recommend next week) where we walk through the eval results and configurables (batching, quantization profile, cache).

Can you confirm who on your side will send the sample prompts and preferred time windows for the demo?

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Ava —

Great questions — answers below and I pasted the relevant excerpts from the benchmark page.

1) p95 latency (2k tokens):
- Hosted API (standard tier, shared): redwood-llama-13b-qa: p50=120ms, p95=320ms at 15 TPS; p99=520ms. redwood-grand-7b: p50=95ms, p95=260ms at 20 TPS.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pool, optimized kernels + batching): redwood-llama-13b-qa: p50=75ms, p95=190ms at sustained 25 TPS. redwood-grand-7b: p50=60ms, p95=150ms at sustained 30 TPS.

2) Quantization & quality regressions:
- We observe small recall/precision shifts when moving from fp16->int8 (particularly on open-ended summarization). For retrieval-augmented QA, the regression is typically <3-5% on our internal NLI/QA evals when using our recommended quantization profile.
- Continuous-batching has minimal impact on output quality — the main tradeoff is tail latency variability; we mitigate this with adaptive batching + per-route latency SLOs.
- We include prompt-level regression alerts in Redwood Optimize so you can gate rollouts by quality thresholds.

Related links and artifacts (public + shared):
- Benchmarks page (public): https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/rdw-2026-0456
- Shared PDF: https://drive.redwood.ai/s/redwood_benchmarks_202602.pdf
- Prompt set we discussed (attached): prompt_set_v1.csv
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/RDW-2026-0456

Marissa — can you provision a hosted trial (48-72h) for Ava Tech on the redwood-grand-7b and redwood-llama-13b-qa variants and add telemetry to capture latency percentiles and hallucination regression metrics? ETA?

Ava / John — if you can send the 100-200 sample prompts and expected outputs, we'll queue the eval job and share a results dashboard within 48 hours.

Thanks,
Alex
